procedural_matters: SWE 77 was represented by Vilma Bobeck
ITA 20 was represented by Jana Germani
Jana Germani (helm of ITA 20) provided video evidence.
Saskia Tidey (crew of GBR 24) gave evidence as a witness for SWE 77.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 5 - 6 knots of wind and flat water.
SWE 77 was sailing upwind close-hauled on starboard.
ITA 20 was sailing upwind close-hauled on port.
The boats were on converging courses.
When the boats were 2 boat lengths apart, ITA 20 started to luff to tack. As she passed head to wind, her speed dropped.
When ITA 20 reached a close-hauled course on starboard tack, SWE 77 overlapped to windward with the bow of SWE 77 1 metre to windwad of the starboard back corner of ITA 20's wing.
Immediately after ITA 20 finished her tack, SWE 77 who was sailing faster, luffed sharply, leading her to crash tack to port.
There was no contact and no boat took a penalty turn.
conclusions: SWE 77's tack was an unseamanlike manoeuvre in the existing conditions.
When acquiring right-of-way through her own actions, ITA 20 failed to initially give SWE 77 room to keep clear, and broke RRS 15.
